While the statement highlights significant near-term downside risks from COVID-19, the FOMC’s swift move to the effective lower bound, large-scale Treasury and MBS purchases, expanded repo operations, discount window easing, and dollar swap lines are consistent with the credit- and bank-lending-channel literature that shows such actions reduce the external finance premium and support credit when balance sheets are strained, thereby cushioning output (e.g., findings on investment sensitivity to cash flow and net worth). In a liquidity-trap environment, balance-sheet policies can bolster aggregate demand when policy rates are at zero, and with survey-based longer-term inflation expectations little changed, the commitment helps stabilize inflation around target. Net effect: tone remains negative given the shock, but tempered by historically forceful, theory-consistent policy support.
